Q: Thank you for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just keep it to the accident and my injuries, if that's okay.
Q: That's fine. For the record, you were the driver of the vehicle that was struck from behind, correct?
A: Yes, I was driving my sedan. I was stopped at a red light in Sugar Land, first car in the lane.
Q: Tell me what happened in your own words.
A: I was waiting for the light to change, and then I felt a hard jolt from behind. My head snapped back and then
forward. The other driver's bumper was pretty much right at my trunk by the time I realized what was happening.
Q: Did the other driver say anything to you at the scene?
A: They apologized and said they looked down at their phone for a second. They seemed shaken up too.
Q: Were you able to drive your car away from the scene?
A: No. The rear of the car was crumpled and the trunk wouldn't close right. A tow truck took it.
Q: When did you first notice pain?
A: Within an hour or so. My right shoulder started aching, and by that evening I couldn't lift my arm above my
shoulder without sharp pain.
Q: Have you seen a doctor or received treatment?
A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic the next day, and they referred me to an orthopedist. I'm starting physical
therapy this week.
Q: Did you have any shoulder problems before this accident?
A: No, not that I can recall. I've been active and never had any treatment for it.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I'm still missing work and I'm worried about how long recovery will take.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
</page>
